survey: A spiral topiary shrub on a lawn, seen from the front at slightly below eye level. The foliage forms four tilted, stacked tiers that get smaller toward a rounded top, and together they read as a continuous spiral. The bottom tier sits in a round, low stone planter ring. Brown soil shows between the foliage and the ring, so the plant is rooted and resting on the ground, not floating. Each tier sits on the one below it with no gaps, so the mass is supported all the way up. The central trunk is hidden by foliage, which is normal for a dense clipped topiary. The planter ring is round and level and lies flat on the grass, where it casts a contact shadow. The background has a clipped hedge and a paved path, both of which sit correctly on the ground.
